messages.subject: inconsistency with new Wave format from tuneR
messages.subject_clean: inconsistency with new Wave format from tuneR
messages.body_plain:
The new version of tuneR (1.0) has support for Wave files which use the WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE header. This is great news for those of us working with 24-bit Wave files.

However, files of this type are returned from readWave() as a different class, i.e. WaveMC instead of Wave. This seems to have the result that functions such as spectro(), spec(), and meanspec(), which normally read the sampling rate directly from the Wave object, require the sampling rate to be specified manually for WaveMC objects. It would be really cool if these functions could deal with WaveMC objects in the same way as Wave objects, so that the same code could handle either.

As an example, I have attached a short vocalization in two formats. AMRE_16.wav is a regular old 16-bit Wave file, while AMRE_24.wav is a 24-bit file with the extensible header.

> AMRE_16 = readWave("AMRE_16.wav")
> AMRE_24 = readWave("AMRE_24.wav")
> AMRE_16

Wave Object
        Number of Samples:      4498
        Duration (seconds):     0.1
        Samplingrate (Hertz):   44100
        Channels (Mono/Stereo): Mono
        PCM (integer format):   TRUE
        Bit (8/16/24/32/64):    16

> AMRE_24

WaveMC Object
        Number of Samples:      4498
        Duration (seconds):     0.1
        Samplingrate (Hertz):   44100
        Number of channels:     1
        PCM (integer format):   TRUE
        Bit (8/16/24/32/64):    24

> spectro(AMRE_16)   # works fine!
> spectro(AMRE_24)
Error in inputw(wave = wave, f = f) :
  argument "f" is missing, with no default
> spectro(AMRE_24, f=44100)  # also works

Best,
Jesse Ross
Research Analyst
Bioacoustics Research Program
Cornell Lab of Ornithology

messages.body_plain:
Awesome, thanks!!

I went ahead and made a minor change to inputw() to address this issue, and it's working for my files. The patch is attached, if you're interested.

However, this is a quick band-aid solution, insofar as it only supports 1- and 2-channel Wave files, the same as the Wave class. Supporting true multi-channel seems like it might require more thought. :)

best,
jesse
